# Opaque Node Identity (schema v28)

> ⚠️ **Status: Draft — awaiting Human Operator approval** (Constitution Art. II). Split out of *The Library Graph* at the Human Operator's direction, 2026-08-05, because it grew its own irreversible step and a blast radius reaching outside the database.
**Parent:** *The Library Graph* (Epic, Approved). This spec implements **one sentence of D2**: *"identity is not a display name."*
## The problem, stated exactly
`EntityProfile.id` is literally `"actor:Name"`. **The display name is the primary key.**
Three things follow, and none is fixable while that is true:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Renaming cascades** | changing a name changes the id, so every reference must be rewritten — which is why a global entity-rename mechanism exists at all |
| **A tag split is impossible** | the Epic's D3 splits a colliding tag into an `action` and an `attribute` node sharing a display name. Both would claim the same key |
| **Aliases stay a special case** | one person with several strings cannot be one node when the string *is* the node |
## D1 — What changes
|  | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | `"actor:Name"` | opaque, stable, never re-derived |
| Display name | the key | an ordinary attribute, freely editable |
| `prefix:Name` | the key | a **legacy input form**, resolved through a lookup index |
```javascript
-- additive first; the old id column is retired last.
ALTER TABLE entity_profiles ADD COLUMN uid TEXT;           -- opaque, every row
ALTER TABLE entity_profiles ADD COLUMN entity_type TEXT;   -- actor | studio | tag | series
ALTER TABLE entity_profiles ADD COLUMN display_name TEXT;  -- was encoded in the id

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX entity_lookup
    ON entity_profiles (entity_type, IFNULL(tag_kind,''), display_name);
```
**Population and re-keying, explicitly:**
```javascript
-- 1. every row gets an id and its name/type unpacked from the old key
UPDATE entity_profiles SET
    uid          = <fresh opaque id per row>,
    entity_type  = substr(id, 1, instr(id,':')-1),
    display_name = substr(id, instr(id,':')+1);

-- 2. every referencing table re-pointed BY JOIN on the old id, not by name
UPDATE video_performer SET performer_id =
    (SELECT uid FROM entity_profiles WHERE entity_profiles.id = video_performer.performer_id);
-- ... identically for video_studio, video_tag, performer_tag,
--     studio_parent (BOTH columns), pending_tag_association, deleted_entities

-- 3. verify: zero rows in any table reference an id that is not a known uid
```
⚠️ **Re-point by joining on the old id, never by re-deriving from the name.** Re-deriving would silently merge two nodes whose names collide — which is exactly the state D3's tag split creates.
⚠️ **`tag_kind`**** is added by v26, not here.** This spec assumes it exists; if v26 has not shipped, the lookup index cannot be created and v28 must not run.
⚠️ **The index is over (type, kind, name) — never over the name alone.** A unique index on name would reject exactly the tag split D3 exists to allow. For performers and studios, where no kind axis exists, the triple degenerates to the name and behaves as before.
## ⚠️ D2 — Three things reference nodes, and all three must move together
This is the whole risk of the spec. Re-keying any one of them alone corrupts the library.
### 1. The edge tables
`video_performer`, `video_studio`, `video_tag`, `performer_tag`, `studio_parent`, `pending_tag_association` — re-pointed to `uid` in the same migration. **Re-keying profiles without the edges orphans the entire graph.**
### 2. `deleted_entities` — the one that fails silently
Tombstones are keyed `actor:Name`. A tombstone still carrying an old-style id **stops matching the entity it was meant to suppress**, so the deletion resurrects on the next federation sync — the precise failure that table was built to prevent.
⚠️ **This failure is invisible at migration time.** Nothing breaks, no error is raised; a deleted entity simply reappears later, in the other library, looking like a sync bug.
### 3. Every photo on disk — the one that is irreversible
`ProfileImageNaming` derives each filename from `safeId(for:)` — the entity id with `:` replaced — so profile and gallery images sit on disk as `actor_Name.jpg`.
| File | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary photo | `actor_Name.jpg` | `<uid>.jpg` |
| Gallery photo | `actor_Name_<sha256(token)>.jpg` | `<uid>_<sha256(token)>.jpg` |
⭐ **Only the prefix changes.** The gallery token hash is derived from the source URL, not from the entity, so it is carried across untouched — which means the mapping is mechanical and a gallery photo's identity within a profile survives.
**Re-keying nodes without renaming those files orphans every profile photo and every gallery image in the library.** These are downloaded assets, not regenerable thumbnails: `.vilmbackup` holds them, but the app cannot rebuild them from the source without re-fetching.
## D3 — The photo rename is two-phase, because disk and database fail independently
| Phase | Action | On failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Copy** every image to its `uid`-derived name. Both names now exist | re-runnable; nothing lost |
| 2 | **Verify** the new-name count equals the old-name count | abort; database untouched |
| 3 | **Commit** the id change in the database | atomic transaction |
| 4 | **Delete** the old-named files | orphans are harmless and re-runnable |
⚠️ **The order is the safety.** Committing the database before copying the files would desynchronise disk from catalogue with no way back — the same class of failure as the Epic's V1, one layer down and irreversible.
💡 **Disk cost is temporary but real.** Both copies exist between phases 1 and 4.
**Pre-flight check, run before phase 1 copies anything:**
```javascript
free_space  >  (total bytes of all profile + gallery images) * 1.1  +  100 MB
```
The 10% margin covers filesystem overhead and images added between measurement and copy; the flat 100 MB covers the database's own growth during the migration. **Below that, the migration refuses to start** rather than failing part-way with both copies half-present.
### Phase 4 is interruptible and idempotent
Phase 4 deletes old-named files after the commit. Interrupted, it leaves some old names present — which is **harmless**: the database already points at the new names, so those files are unreferenced orphans. Re-running deletes what remains. ⚠️ **Phase 4 must therefore be re-runnable without checking whether it ran before**, and must never treat a missing old-named file as an error.
## ⚠️ D4 — A uid is LOCAL; federation still identifies by name
The app federates across libraries, and **a uid minted in one library means nothing in another.** Two libraries holding the same performer will mint different uids for them.
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Within a library | `uid` is identity |
| **Between libraries** | **(entity type, tag kind, display name)** remains the identity, exactly as today |
| A tombstone crossing libraries | matched by that same triple, not by uid |
⚠️ **This is why ****`display_name`**** is a first-class column and not merely a label.** Federation, AKA reconciliation and sync all continue to resolve by name; what changes is that *within* a library the name is no longer load-bearing for edges.
⚠️ **A migrated library must sync with an un-migrated one.** Both sides exchange the name triple, so no version negotiation is needed — but this only holds while the sync payload never carries a raw id. **Verify that before shipping**; a payload containing `actor:Name` today would be read as a uid tomorrow.
## D5 — Sequencing
**This is Phase D work in the Epic's ordering and must not run early.**
| Prerequisite | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Epic Phase A complete | never migrate identity while writes are still being silently dropped |
| The tag vocabulary classified | the split this enables is meaningless until kinds exist |
| Studio conflicts resolved | `video_studio` cardinality must be satisfiable first |
| A verified `.vilmbackup` taken immediately before | the only true rollback for phase 3 onward |
🚨 **Do not run this during the relocation work.** Both touch the filesystem at scale, and a failure while both are in flight is unattributable — you would not know whether a missing file was a move or a re-key.
## Test strategy (Constitution Art. III)
- **V1 — Nothing is lost.** Every profile retains every field; the row count is unchanged; each former `prefix:Name` resolves to the right node through the lookup index.
- **V2 — The split becomes possible.** Two tags sharing a display name with different kinds both exist, both resolve, and the unique index accepts them. Run against a fixture containing a deliberate collision — the case that is impossible before this migration.
- **V3 — Every edge follows.** After migration each edge table references `uid`, and every relationship that existed before still exists, counted per table rather than in aggregate.
- **V4 — Tombstones still suppress.** An entity deleted before the migration stays deleted after it, **and after a federation sync** — the assertion that catches the silent failure.
- **V5 — Every photo resolves.** Each profile and gallery image resolves for the node it belonged to, verified by count against the pre-migration set. A photo that no longer resolves is data loss, not a cache miss.
- **V6 — Interruption is safe at every phase.** Killed during phases 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively, the library is left consistent and the migration is re-runnable. Asserted per phase, because they fail differently.
- **V7 — A full volume aborts cleanly.** With insufficient free space the migration refuses before copying anything, rather than failing part-way.
- **V9 — A migrated library syncs with an un-migrated one.** Federation between the two resolves the same entities in both directions, creates no duplicates, and honours tombstones on both sides. Asserted in both directions, because they fail differently.
- **V10 — Re-pointing never merges two nodes.** Against a fixture holding two distinct nodes whose display names collide, every edge lands on the node it started from. This is the assertion that catches a re-derive-by-name implementation.
- **V11 — Phase 4 is idempotent.** Run twice, or resumed after a kill, it completes without error and treats an already-deleted file as success.
- **V8 — Renaming becomes free.** After migration, renaming a node changes one row and moves no edges — the property this entire spec exists to buy (Epic T7).
## Evidence
`EntityProfile.id` format and `ProfileImageNaming.safeId(for:)` read at commit `adb457a`, 2026-08-05. `EntityTombstone` is keyed by entity id and exists for federation sync. Library scale: 1,386 performer profiles, of which 1,204 carry full birth dates; gallery photo counts are per-profile and unmeasured for this spec — **measure before sizing phase 1's disk requirement.**
## 🚨 D6 — v28 must NOT be a registered migration
Added 2026-08-06, from reading `LibraryStore.init(at:)`. This follows directly from the operator's observation that **D5's prerequisites are per library, not global.**
`LibraryStore(at:)` calls `migrate()` on open, and the migrator runs every unapplied migration immediately. So a `registerMigration("v28")` block would run **the moment any library is opened** — including one whose prerequisites are not met.
Concretely, with the phone library cleaned up and the drive library still holding 63 two-studio videos: registering v28 would migrate the phone library correctly and then migrate the **drive** library the instant it is attached, bypassing every gate this spec defines — the studio-conflict prerequisite, the free-space pre-flight, the four-phase photo copy, and the requirement for a verified backup taken immediately before.
⭐ **Therefore v28 is an operator-invoked, per-library operation**, not a schema migration. Precedent exists: *Migrate Episode Info* is invoked from Settings → Maintenance and runs against the selected library only.
| Part | Where it belongs |
| --- | --- |
| Additive columns (`uid`, `entity_type`, `display_name`) and the lookup index | a registered migration — additive, reversible, harmless on any library |
| Minting uids, re-pointing edges and tombstones, renaming photos, retiring the old id | **operator-invoked**, gated on the pre-flight checks, run per library |
⚠️ Splitting it this way also makes the mixed state D4 already designs for **explicit rather than incidental**: a library can carry the new columns while still being keyed the old way, and D4's rule — federation resolves by the name triple, never by uid — is what keeps that safe.
⚠️ **This changes the migration numbering.** The additive half is a migration; the re-keying half is not, so calling the whole thing "schema v28" is now imprecise. The additive migration is the only part with a version number.
### Also affected by v30
*Temporal Edges* (phase 2) shipped first, so `studio_parent` can now hold **several rows per studio** — one current, plus closed historical periods.
- The re-pointing statements are unaffected: they update **by column**, not by row.
- 🚨 **V3 must be re-derived.** It asserts per-table edge counts before and after, and `studio_parent`'s count is no longer bounded by the number of studios.
- The partial unique index `studio_parent_current` is over `studio_id`, which the re-keying rewrites in place. Verify it still holds **after** re-pointing, since re-pointing two former parents of one studio to the same uid cannot create a second open row — but that reasoning should be asserted, not assumed.
